en: be wary of; be on guard against; watch out for

examples.en: You should be wary of strangers.
Our puppy is wary of guests.

examples.ko: 그는 처음 만난 사람을 경계하는 편이에요.
examples.en: He tends to be on guard with people he first meets.
The news told people to beware of scam calls.
The cat approached slowly, wary of me.
Don't be so guarded, let's talk comfortably.

explain: '조심하다'는 일반적인 주의이고, '경계하다'는 나쁜 일이 생길까 봐 의심하며 지켜보는 느낌이 강해요. 사람, 동물, 위험한 것을 목적어로 자주 써요. '경계를 풀다'처럼 명사 '경계'와 같이 쓰는 말도 많아요.
explain_en: 조심하다 is general carefulness, while 경계하다 feels more suspicious, as if watching for something bad to happen. Its objects are usually people, animals or dangers. The noun 경계 also appears in set phrases like '경계를 풀다'.

examples.en: What are you thinking so hard about?

examples.ko: 그는 창밖을 보며 골똘히 고민에 잠겼어요.
examples.en: He looked out the window, lost in deep thought.

examples.ko: 골똘히 생각한 끝에 좋은 방법이 떠올랐어요.
examples.en: After thinking hard, a good idea came to me.
The child is staring intently at the puzzle.

examples.ko: 골똘히 생각하느라 버스에서 내릴 곳을 지나쳤어요.
examples.en: I was so lost in thought that I missed my stop on the bus.
My friend is writing something down with great concentration.

explain: 생각, 고민 같은 말과 함께 써서 한 가지에 깊이 빠진 모습을 나타내요. '곰곰'은 차분히 되짚어 보는 느낌이고, '골똘히'는 다른 건 신경 쓰지 못할 만큼 몰두한 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It goes with words like 생각 and 고민 to show someone deeply absorbed in one thing. '곰곰' feels like calmly going back over something, while '골똘히' suggests being so engrossed that you notice little else.

en: object of interest; topic of interest

examples.ko: 요즘 제 가장 큰 관심거리는 요리예요.
examples.en: My biggest interest these days is cooking.
That rumor became the talk of the town.

examples.ko: 아이들에게 새로운 관심거리를 찾아 주는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: It's important to help children find new things to be interested in.
The new product has become something people are curious about.

examples.ko: 다른 사람의 사생활이 관심거리가 되는 건 싫어요.
examples.en: I don't like it when other people's private lives become a topic of interest.
Besides your hobby, do you have other interests?

explain: '관심사'는 한 사람이 평소 가진 관심 분야에 가깝고, '관심거리'는 사람들의 관심이 쏠리는 일이나 화제에 가까워요. 비슷한 뜻으로 '화제'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: '관심사' leans toward a person's usual area of interest, while '관심거리' leans toward a matter or topic that draws attention. '화제' is also commonly used with a similar sense.

examples.en: I decided to keep that story buried in my heart.

examples.ko: 오래된 비밀을 평생 묻어둘 수는 없어요.
examples.en: You can't keep an old secret buried for a lifetime.
If you bury potatoes in soil, they last a long time.

examples.ko: 아이는 상처를 혼자 묻어둔 채 지냈어요.
examples.en: The child kept the hurt buried inside and went on living.

examples.ko: 그 문제를 계속 묻어둬서 더 커졌어요.
examples.en: We kept burying that problem, so it got bigger.

examples.ko: 좋은 아이디어를 묻어두지 말고 말해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't keep your good idea to yourself; say it out loud.

explain: 땅에 묻어서 그대로 두는 것뿐 아니라, 말이나 문제를 꺼내지 않고 그냥 두는 뜻으로도 많이 써요. 이때는 '덮어두다'와 비슷하고, 반대로 '꺼내다', '털어놓다'와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Besides literally burying something and leaving it, it is often used for leaving a word or problem unspoken. In that sense it is close to '덮어두다', and its opposites are '꺼내다' and '털어놓다'.

examples.en: At first I was half-skeptical about that ad.
I tried the medicine with mixed feelings of trust and doubt.

examples.ko: 그 이야기가 사실인지 저는 아직도 반신반의예요.
examples.en: I'm still half in doubt about whether that story is true.
I was unsure, but when I went myself, it was true.
Everyone waited for the result, torn between belief and doubt.

examples.ko: 반신반의인 사람이 많아서 설명이 더 필요해요.
examples.en: Many people are unsure, so more explanation is needed.

explain: 절반은 믿고 절반은 의심하는 마음을 말하는 사자성어예요. 보통 '반신반의하다'로 쓰고, 명사로는 '반신반의예요/반신반의였어요'처럼 말해요. 일상에서는 '긴가민가하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a four-character expression for half believing and half doubting. It is usually used as the verb '반신반의하다', and as a noun in forms like '반신반의예요/반신반의였어요'. In daily talk people also say '긴가민가하다'.

examples.ko: 아기가 엄마를 보고 벙실벙실 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: The baby is looking at Mom and smiling happily.
Grandpa smiled broadly as he looked at his grandchild.

examples.ko: 상을 받은 동생이 하루 종일 벙실벙실 웃고 다녀요.
examples.en: My younger sibling who won the prize goes around smiling all day.
The children saw the presents and beamed.

examples.ko: 벙실벙실 웃는 얼굴을 보니 저도 행복해졌어요.
examples.en: Seeing that beaming face made me happy too.

examples.ko: 그는 칭찬을 듣고 벙실벙실 기분 좋게 웃었어요.
examples.en: He heard the compliment and smiled happily.

explain: 입을 크게 벌리고 소리 없이 부드럽게 웃는 모습이에요. 아기나 마음씨 좋은 사람의 웃음에 잘 어울려요. '방실방실'은 더 작고 귀여운 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It shows a soft, silent smile with the mouth wide open. It suits a baby or a good-natured person. '방실방실' feels smaller and cuter.

examples.en: Do you have a plan in mind for solving this problem?

examples.ko: 김 팀장님은 이미 나름의 복안을 갖고 계세요.
examples.en: Team Leader Kim already has a plan of his own in mind.
I can't tell you my plan yet.

examples.ko: 정부는 새 정책에 대한 복안을 발표했어요.
examples.en: The government announced its plan for the new policy.

examples.ko: 아무 복안 없이 시작하면 나중에 힘들어요.
examples.en: If you start without any plan in mind, it gets hard later.

examples.ko: 그 일은 복안대로 잘 진행되고 있어요.
examples.en: That work is going well, just as planned.

explain: '복안이 있다/없다'처럼 쓰는 일이 많고, 아직 밝히지 않은 속마음의 계획이라는 느낌이 있어요. 그냥 '계획'보다 격식 있어서 뉴스나 회의에서 자주 들려요. 친구끼리는 '생각이 있어' 정도로 말해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '복안이 있다/없다' and feels like a plan one keeps to oneself and hasn't revealed yet. It is more formal than '계획' and is heard in news and meetings. Among friends people would just say something like '생각이 있어'.

examples.en: The sunlight was strong, so I put on tinted glasses.
It's hard to walk along the beach without tinted glasses.

examples.ko: 이 색안경이 얼굴에 정말 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: These tinted glasses really suit your face.
I left my tinted glasses in the car when I got out.
The glare was bright, so I wore tinted glasses while driving.

examples.ko: 가게에서 마음에 드는 색안경을 하나 골랐어요.
examples.en: I picked out a pair of tinted glasses I liked at the store.

explain: 눈을 보호하려고 쓰는 짙은 색 안경이에요. 일상에서는 '선글라스'라고도 하는데, '색안경'은 편견을 가진 시선을 말할 때도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Don't look at someone with prejudice just because they're a foreigner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선입견이나 편견을 가지고 어떤 사람이나 일을 바라본다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means looking at a person or matter with preconceptions or bias.
phrases.en_equiv: view through tinted glasses; look with a biased eye

explain_en: It is dark-tinted glasses worn to protect the eyes. In daily talk people also say '선글라스', but '색안경' is the word often used for a prejudiced way of looking at someone.

examples.en: I deliberated for a long time about whether to move.
It's an important decision, so please think it over carefully.

examples.ko: 그는 숙고한 끝에 회사를 떠나기로 했어요.
examples.en: After careful consideration, he decided to leave the company.

examples.ko: 숙고하지 않고 계약서에 서명하면 나중에 후회해요.
examples.en: If you sign a contract without thinking it through, you'll regret it later.
I'll weigh the various opinions and come to a conclusion.
The teacher thought for a long while and then spoke.

explain: '생각하다'보다 신중하고 오래 따져 본다는 느낌이에요. '고민하다'는 걱정하며 힘들어하는 느낌이 있지만 '숙고하다'는 차분히 따져 보는 느낌이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '곰곰이 생각하다'라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It means thinking carefully and for a long time, more than plain '생각하다'. '고민하다' carries a feeling of worry and struggle, while '숙고하다' is calm weighing of options. In daily talk people often say '곰곰이 생각하다'.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 살던 집이 아련히 떠올라요.
examples.en: The house I lived in as a child comes faintly to mind.
A bell could be heard faintly from far away.
There is one song I remember dimly.
The mountain looked hazy in the fog.
I vaguely and wistfully recall my first love's face.

examples.ko: 아련히 남아 있는 그날의 냄새가 그리워요.
examples.en: I miss the faint scent of that day that still lingers.

explain: 또렷하지 않게 멀고 희미한데, 그리운 마음이 함께 들어 있어요. '희미하게'는 단순히 흐린 것이고, '아련히'는 추억이나 소리에 감정이 담길 때 잘 어울려요. 형용사 '아련하다'는 '아련한 추억'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It means faint and far away, with a touch of longing mixed in. '희미하게' just means unclear, while '아련히' suits memories and sounds that carry emotion. The adjective '아련하다' is used as in '아련한 추억'.

examples.en: I felt relieved after seeing the exam result.
Everyone was relieved to hear the child was safe.

examples.ko: 길을 찾은 뒤에야 안도할 수 있었어요.
examples.en: I could only feel relieved after finding the way.
My parents felt relieved at the news that I had arrived.
When the rain stopped, people had relieved looks.
He took a deep breath, feeling relieved.

explain: '다행이다'는 일이 잘 풀려서 좋다는 마음이고, '안도하다'는 걱정하던 일이 끝나서 마음이 놓이는 모습을 말해요. 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 쓰고, 말할 때는 '마음이 놓이다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 합격 소식을 듣고 안도의 한숨을 쉬었어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정이 끝났을 때 숨을 길게 내쉬는 모습으로 말해요. 실제 한숨이 아니어도 마음이 놓였다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the long breath you let out when a worry ends. It can be used even without an actual sigh, to mean you feel relieved.

explain_en: '다행이다' is feeling glad that things turned out well; '안도하다' describes the moment your mind settles because a worry is over. It is common in writing and news; in speech '마음이 놓이다' is more natural.

examples.en: If a company falls into complacency, it's hard for it to grow.
The boss is very worried about the employees' complacency.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 안일주의 때문에 큰 실수를 했어요.
examples.en: That team made a big mistake because of its take-it-easy attitude.

examples.ko: 이제 안일주의를 버리고 새로운 방법을 찾아봐요.
examples.en: Let's drop the complacency and look for a new method.

examples.ko: 공무원 사회의 안일주의를 비판하는 기사를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read an article criticizing the complacency in the civil service.
We have to be careful not to let complacency spread.

explain: 어렵거나 힘든 일은 피하고 편한 쪽만 택하는 태도를 비판할 때 써요. '무사안일주의'라고도 하고, 회의나 뉴스처럼 조금 딱딱한 자리에서 나와요. 보통 '안일주의에 빠지다', '안일주의를 버리다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is used to criticize an attitude of avoiding hard things and choosing only what is easy. It is also said as '무사안일주의' and appears in somewhat formal settings like meetings and the news. Typical patterns are '안일주의에 빠지다' and '안일주의를 버리다'.

examples.en: Don't guess; find out exactly.

examples.ko: 사람이 백 명쯤 온 것 같다고 어림짐작했어요.
examples.en: I roughly estimated that about a hundred people had come.
My rough guess wasn't far off.

examples.ko: 거리를 어림짐작해서 걸음 수를 세어 봤어요.
examples.en: I estimated the distance and counted my steps.
It's risky to decide things based only on guesswork.
Rough guesses often miss the mark.

explain: 정확한 계산이나 확인 없이 대충 헤아려 맞히는 것에 써요. '어림짐작으로', '어림짐작하다'처럼 쓰고, 정확하지 않다는 느낌이 있어서 중요한 결정에는 안 좋은 방법으로 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for guessing roughly without exact calculation or checking. It appears as '어림짐작으로' or '어림짐작하다', and carries a sense of imprecision, so it is often mentioned as a poor basis for important decisions.

examples.en: His explanation is a little questionable.
The results came out so fast that I was doubtful.
If anything seems doubtful, ask right away.
I got a strange and dubious phone call.

examples.ko: 뉴스 내용이 의문스러워서 다른 곳도 찾아봤어요.
examples.en: The news content seemed dubious, so I checked other sources too.

examples.ko: 의문스러울 때는 자료를 한 번 더 확인해요.
examples.en: When in doubt, I check the data once more.

explain: '이상하다'는 보통과 다르다는 느낌이고, '의문스럽다'는 믿기 어렵거나 이유를 잘 모르겠다는 느낌이에요. 말할 때는 '수상하다', '이상하다'를 더 많이 써요. 활용은 '의문스러워요', '의문스러운'처럼 ㅂ이 바뀌어요.
explain_en: 이상하다 means different from normal; 의문스럽다 means hard to believe or unclear why. In speech 수상하다 and 이상하다 are used more. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective: 의문스러워요, 의문스러운.

examples.en: After I took the medicine, my cough calmed down.
Let's talk again once you've calmed down.
The protest settled down as night came.
We started the meeting in a calmer atmosphere.
Prices seem likely to settle soon.
When the child is held, the crying settles.

explain: '진정하다'는 내가 마음을 가라앉히는 것이고, '진정되다'는 흥분·통증·소란이 저절로 가라앉는 것이에요. '진정하세요'는 '진정하다'의 명령이라 흥분한 사람에게 해요. '진정되다'는 사람에게 명령하지 않아요.
explain_en: '진정하다' is you calming yourself; '진정되다' is excitement, pain or commotion subsiding on its own. '진정하세요' (calm down!) comes from '진정하다'; you don't give commands with '진정되다'.

examples.ko: 추리 소설을 읽으면 시간이 빨리 가요.
examples.en: Time flies when I read a mystery novel.
The detective began reasoning from a small clue.
His deduction was accurate, so everyone was surprised.

examples.ko: 추리의 재미는 범인을 맞히는 데 있어요.
examples.en: The fun of a mystery is in guessing the culprit.
There were few clues, so the deduction had limits.
This game needs deduction and a way with words.

explain: '추리 소설', '추리 영화'처럼 이야기 장르 이름으로 가장 자주 나와요. '추론'은 논리나 공부에서 쓰는 말이고, '추리'는 사건과 범인처럼 단서를 모아 짐작할 때 어울려요. 단서 없이 막연히 하는 것은 '짐작'이에요.
explain_en: Most often seen as a story genre, as in '추리 소설' and '추리 영화'. '추론' is used in logic and academics, while 추리 fits gathering clues about a case or culprit. Guessing with no clues is '짐작'.

examples.en: I feel pathetic when I put off my homework.

examples.ko: 같은 실수를 또 한 제가 한심스러웠어요.
examples.en: I felt pathetic for making the same mistake again.
That kind of behavior looks truly pitiful.
Please stop the pathetic excuses.
My friend looked at me with a look that said I was pathetic.

examples.ko: 아무것도 안 하고 하루를 보낸 게 한심스럽게 느껴져요.
examples.en: Spending the day doing nothing feels pathetic.

explain: '한심하다'와 거의 같아요. 남에게 직접 말하면 모욕이 되니 조심하세요. 자기 자신에게 쓰면 스스로를 탓하는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '한심하다'. Saying it directly to someone is insulting, so be careful. Used about yourself, it feels like blaming yourself.
